title: Bladder drugs: urgency, voiding and the outlet
ariaLabel: Schematic of bladder control: parasympathetic input to M3 receptors contracts the detrusor and causes urgency, beta-3 receptors relax the detrusor so it stores more, and alpha-1 receptors at the outlet keep it tight. Antimuscarinics such as oxybutynin block M3 receptors, mirabegron stimulates beta-3 receptors, and tamsulosin blocks alpha-1 receptors at the outlet.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Vagal drive
nodes.info: Acetylcholine acting on M3 receptors of the bladder wall.

nodes.label: Detrusor contraction
nodes.info: Bladder wall contraction that causes urgency.

nodes.label: Sympathetic input
nodes.info: Noradrenaline acting on beta-3 receptors of the detrusor.

nodes.label: Detrusor relaxation
nodes.info: Relaxation that lets the bladder fill.

nodes.label: Outlet tone
nodes.info: Alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck keep the outlet tight.

nodes.label: Outlet tight
nodes.info: A tight outlet causes poor flow and, with an irritable bladder, urgency and incomplete emptying.

nodes.label: Bladder symptoms
nodes.info: A teaching score for urgency, frequency and poor flow.

edges.label: M3 receptors
edges.info: Antimuscarinics (oxybutynin, tolterodine, solifenacin) block M3 receptors, so the detrusor contracts less and urgency falls. Dry mouth and constipation are common.

edges.label: beta-3 receptors
edges.info: Mirabegron stimulates beta-3 receptors, relaxing the detrusor during storage so the bladder holds more.

edges.label: alpha-1 receptors
edges.info: Tamsulosin and other alpha-1 blockers relax the outlet so urine flows more easily, helping obstruction from an enlarged prostate. Postural hypotension can occur.
A tight outlet adds to bladder symptoms.

sources: Where each class acts. Antimuscarinics block M3 receptors, mirabegron stimulates beta-3 receptors, and alpha-1 blockers relax the bladder outlet. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (own figure), desmopressin for nocturia, botulinum toxin, bladder training, urinary retention, blood pressure effects of mirabegron, anticholinergic burden and cognition, dry mouth and adverse effects are left out. Bladder symptoms are drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
